source.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֖ם שְׁכֶ֑ם כִּ֥י שְׁכֶ֛ם בָּ֥א כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהַמְלִ֥יךְ אֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Rehoboam [to] Shechem, for [to] Shechem had come all Israel to make king him.

en.L: And Rehoboam went [to] Shechem, for all Israel had come [to] Shechem to make him king.
en.B: Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel had gathered at Shechem to make him king.
en.R: Rehoboam went to the town of Shechem. All the people of Israel had gathered there to make him their king.

decisions.choice: Shechem: the old meeting place of the northern tribes
decisions.reason: Shechem lay in the hill country of Ephraim (verse 25). Joshua gathered the tribes there to renew the covenant (Joshua 24:1, 25), and Abimelech was made king there (Judges 9:6). Rehoboam goes to the northern tribes; they do not come to him in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: to make him king: to accept him as their king
decisions.reason: Solomon's son already reigned in Jerusalem (11:43), but the tribes of Israel still had to accept him. The elders of Israel had made a covenant with David before they anointed him king over them (2 Samuel 5:1-3), and the meeting at Shechem expects something similar.

decisions.choice: the town of Shechem; their king
decisions.reason: Readable says that Shechem is a town and makes clear whose king Rehoboam was to be.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ׀יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֗ט וְהוּא֙ עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ בְמִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּרַ֔ח מִפְּנֵ֖י הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב יָרָבְעָ֖ם בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when heard Jeroboam son of Nebat, and he [was] still in Egypt, where he had fled from [the] face of the king Solomon, and dwelt Jeroboam in Egypt.

en.L: And it happened, when Jeroboam son of Nebat heard [it] (and he [was] still in Egypt, where he had fled from the presence of King Solomon), that Jeroboam stayed in Egypt.
en.B: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about it, he was still in Egypt, where he had taken refuge from King Solomon, and he remained in Egypt.
en.R: Jeroboam son of Nebat heard the news while he was still in Egypt. He had run away there from King Solomon, and he stayed there.

decisions.choice: Jeroboam had fled to Egypt from Solomon
decisions.reason: Jeroboam, one of Solomon's officials, was told by the prophet Ahijah that he would rule ten tribes; Solomon tried to kill him, and he fled to Shishak king of Egypt and stayed there until Solomon died (11:26-40).

decisions.choice: and Jeroboam stayed in Egypt
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "and Jeroboam stayed (or lived) in Egypt". The parallel in 2 Chronicles 10:2 reads "and Jeroboam returned from Egypt"; the two verbs differ only in their vowels, and Chronicles adds "from". The Hebrew text of Kings is followed: Jeroboam stayed where he was until the tribes sent for him (verse 3).

decisions.choice: heard [it]: news of Solomon's death and the meeting at Shechem
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. What Jeroboam heard is clear from the verses before: Solomon had died and Rehoboam had become king (11:43), and Israel was gathering at Shechem (verse 1).

decisions.choice: parentheses round the clause about Egypt
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets a background clause in the middle of the sentence. Literal marks it off so that the main line, "when Jeroboam heard ... Jeroboam stayed in Egypt", can be followed.

source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ וַיִּקְרְאוּ־ל֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֥א יָרָבְעָ֖ם וְכָל־קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶל־רְחַבְעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they sent and called him, and came Jeroboam and all [the] assembly of Israel and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,

en.L: And they sent and called him, and Jeroboam and all the assembly of Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
en.B: So they sent and summoned him, and Jeroboam and the whole assembly of Israel came and said to Rehoboam,
en.R: So the people sent for him. Then Jeroboam and the whole gathering of Israel came and said to Rehoboam,

decisions.choice: they sent: the tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; it is the people of Israel gathered at Shechem (verse 1), who call Jeroboam back to speak for them.

decisions.choice: the assembly of Israel: the tribes gathered as one body
decisions.reason: The word names the people assembled for a public act, as when Israel gathered before Solomon at the dedication of the temple (8:14, 22). Here the gathered tribes speak to the king together.

decisions.choice: came: the form marked to be read aloud is singular
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) and the form the scribes marked to be read aloud (qere) differ in the verb "came", between plural and singular. The singular agrees with Jeroboam, named first. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: Jeroboam takes part in the meeting, though verse 20 tells of his return later
decisions.reason: Verses 3 and 12 have Jeroboam lead the people, while verse 20 says that Israel heard he had returned and then called him to the assembly. Verse 20 may look back on the same events from the side of the northern tribes. The old Greek translation does not name Jeroboam in this meeting.

decisions.choice: the whole gathering of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable uses "gathering" for the assembly, as the Numbers to Ruth terms allow.

source.text: אָבִ֖יךָ הִקְשָׁ֣ה אֶת־עֻלֵּ֑נוּ וְאַתָּ֡ה עַתָּ֣ה הָקֵל֩ מֵעֲבֹדַ֨ת אָבִ֜יךָ הַקָּשָׁ֗ה וּמֵעֻלּ֧וֹ הַכָּבֵ֛ד אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן עָלֵ֖ינוּ וְנַעַבְדֶֽךָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Your father made hard our yoke; and you, now, lighten from [the] service of your father the hard and from his yoke the heavy which he put on us, and we will serve you.

en.L: "Your father made our yoke hard. And you, now, lighten [some] of the hard service of your father and of his heavy yoke that he put on us, and we will serve you."
en.B: "Your father made our yoke hard. Now ease the harsh labor your father demanded and the heavy yoke he laid on us, and we will serve you."
en.R: "Your father made life hard for us. He put a heavy load on us, like a heavy yoke on an ox. Now make our hard work easier and our load lighter, and we will serve you."

decisions.choice: yoke: the burden of the king's demands
decisions.reason: A yoke is the wooden bar laid on the necks of oxen so that they can pull. Here it stands for what Solomon required of his people: forced labor on his buildings (5:27-28; 9:15; 11:28) and the food supplied for his court (5:2-8).

decisions.choice: service: work owed to the king
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for work or service; with "hard" it recalls Israel's hard service in Egypt (Exodus 1:14; 6:9). The people describe Solomon's rule in the words used of Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: lighten some of: a request for relief, not for an end to all service
decisions.reason: The preposition "from" means "part of". The people ask the king to reduce the load, and they promise to serve him if he does.

decisions.choice: we will serve you: loyalty on terms
decisions.reason: The tribes offer to accept Rehoboam as king on a condition. Their loyalty depends on how he answers.

decisions.choice: like a heavy yoke on an ox
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the yoke once and then speaks of a load.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם לְכ֥וּ עֹ֛ד שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יָמִ֖ים וְשׁ֣וּבוּ אֵלָ֑י וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Go yet three days and return to me. And went the people.

en.L: And he said to them, "Go [away] yet three days, and return to me." And the people went.
en.B: He said to them, "Go away for three days, then come back to me." So the people left.
en.R: Rehoboam answered, "Go away for three days. Then come back to me." So the people left.

decisions.choice: for three days: until the third day
decisions.reason: The people come back "on the third day" (verse 12), so the three days are counted with the first and last included, as was usual.

decisions.choice: Rehoboam answered
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

source.text: וַיִּוָּעַ֞ץ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם אֶת־הַזְּקֵנִים֙ אֲשֶׁר־הָי֣וּ עֹמְדִ֗ים אֶת־פְּנֵי֙ שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה אָבִ֔יו בִּֽהְיֹת֥וֹ חַ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר אֵ֚יךְ אַתֶּ֣ם נֽוֹעָצִ֔ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־הָֽעָם־הַזֶּ֖ה דָּבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And consulted the king Rehoboam with the elders who had been standing before Solomon his father while he was alive, saying, How you counsel to bring back [to] this people word?

en.L: And King Rehoboam took counsel with the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was alive, saying, "How do you counsel [me] to return a word to this people?"
en.B: King Rehoboam then consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon while he was alive. "What answer do you advise me to give this people?" he asked.
en.R: Then King Rehoboam asked for advice from the older men who had served his father Solomon while he was alive. He asked them, "How should I answer these people?"

decisions.choice: the elders: older men who had been Solomon's advisers
decisions.reason: The word means older men. Here they are senior members of the court who had served Solomon, set against the young men who had grown up with Rehoboam (verse 8); they are not the elders of the tribes.

decisions.choice: stood before: served as attendants and advisers
decisions.reason: To stand before a king is to wait on him and be ready to serve him (1:2; 10:8).

decisions.choice: return a word: give an answer
decisions.reason: "Bring back a word" is the usual Hebrew way of saying "answer"; it returns in verses 9 and 16.

decisions.choice: older men
decisions.reason: Readable says "older men" so that readers do not think of the leaders of the tribes.

source.text: וַיְדַבְּר֨וּאֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר אִם־הַ֠יּוֹם תִּֽהְיֶה־עֶ֜בֶד לָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וַֽעֲבַדְתָּ֔ם וַעֲנִיתָ֕ם וְדִבַּרְתָּ֥ אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם דְּבָרִ֣ים טוֹבִ֑ים וְהָי֥וּ לְךָ֛ עֲבָדִ֖ים כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they spoke to him, saying, If today you will be a servant to this people and serve them and answer them and speak to them good words, then they will be to you servants all the days.

en.L: And they spoke to him, saying, "If today you will be a slave to this people and serve them, and answer them and speak good words to them, then they will be slaves to you all the days."
en.B: They answered him, "If today you will be a servant to this people and serve them, and answer them with kind words, they will always be your servants."
en.R: They told him, "If you will be a servant to these people today and serve them, and if you give them a kind answer, they will always be your servants."

decisions.choice: be a servant to this people, and they will be your servants
decisions.reason: The elders' advice turns on one word: if the king will serve the people for a day, they will serve him for good. The king rules best by serving those he rules (compare Deuteronomy 17:14-20).

decisions.choice: good words: a kind and favorable answer
decisions.reason: "Good words" are gracious words that grant what is asked. The phrase can also mean a promise of good terms.

decisions.choice: today: on this day of decision
decisions.reason: The elders contrast one day of yielding with "all the days" of loyalty that would follow.

decisions.choice: they spoke: the form marked to be read aloud is plural
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) have "he spoke"; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "they spoke", agreeing with the elders. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets out for this word, Literal keeps "slave" and Balanced and Readable say "servant". The point is service, not ownership.

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲזֹ֛ב אֶת־עֲצַ֥ת הַזְּקֵנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְעָצֻ֑הוּ וַיִּוָּעַ֗ץ אֶת־הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר גָּדְל֣וּ אִתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָעֹמְדִ֖ים לְפָנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he abandoned the counsel of the elders which they counseled him, and consulted with the young men who had grown up with him, who [were] the ones standing before him.

en.L: And he forsook the counsel of the elders that they had counseled him, and he took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him, who [were] standing before him.
en.B: But he rejected the advice the elders had given him and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and now served him.
en.R: But Rehoboam did not follow the older men's advice. Instead he asked the young men who had grown up with him and now served him.

decisions.choice: forsook: set aside, rejected
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave or abandon. Rehoboam does not merely disagree with the elders' advice; he throws it aside.

decisions.choice: the young men: Rehoboam's companions of his own age
decisions.reason: The word usually means children or boys. Rehoboam was forty-one when he became king (14:21), so these are not boys; calling them by this word may hint at their lack of judgment.

decisions.choice: standing before him: serving him
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, to stand before the king is to serve him. These young men now held places at Rehoboam's court.

decisions.choice: did not follow
decisions.reason: Readable puts "forsook" in plain words and names Rehoboam.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם מָ֚ה אַתֶּ֣ם נֽוֹעָצִ֔ים וְנָשִׁ֥יב דָּבָ֖ר אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבְּר֤וּ אֵלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הָקֵל֙ מִן־הָעֹ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן אָבִ֖יךָ עָלֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, What you counsel, and we will bring back word [to] this people who have spoken to me, saying, Lighten from the yoke which put your father on us?

en.L: And he said to them, "What do you counsel, that we may return a word to this people who have spoken to me, saying, 'Lighten [some] of the yoke that your father put on us'?"
en.B: He asked them, "What do you advise? How should we answer this people who have said to me, 'Lighten the yoke your father put on us'?"
en.R: He asked them, "What do you advise? How should we answer these people? They said to me, 'Make the load your father put on us lighter.'"

decisions.choice: we: Rehoboam counts the young men in with himself
decisions.reason: To the elders Rehoboam said "to answer" (verse 6); to the young men he says "that we may answer". He treats them as partners in the decision.

decisions.choice: the people's request is repeated in short
decisions.reason: Rehoboam sums up the request of verse 4 in a few words and leaves out the people's promise to serve him.

source.text: וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר גָּדְל֣וּ אִתּוֹ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ כֹּֽה־תֹאמַ֣ר לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֡ה אֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבְּר֨וּ אֵלֶ֜יךָ לֵאמֹ֗ר אָבִ֨יךָ֙ הִכְבִּ֣יד אֶת־עֻלֵּ֔נוּ וְאַתָּ֖ה הָקֵ֣ל מֵעָלֵ֑ינוּ כֹּ֚ה תְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם קָֽטָנִּ֥י עָבָ֖ה מִמָּתְנֵ֥י אָבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke to him the young men who had grown up with him, saying, Thus you will say to this people who spoke to you, saying, Your father made heavy our yoke, and you lighten [it] from on us; thus you will speak to them, My little [finger] [is] thick more than [the] loins of my father.

en.L: And the young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, "Thus you shall say to this people who spoke to you, saying, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you, lighten [it] from on us'; thus you shall speak to them: 'My little [finger] is thicker than the loins of my father.
en.B: The young men who had grown up with him answered, "This people said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you must make it lighter for us.' Give them this answer: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.
en.R: The young men who had grown up with him answered, "These people said to you, 'Your father put a heavy load on us. Make it lighter for us.' So tell them this: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist! I will be much harder on you than he was.

decisions.choice: my little finger is thicker than my father's loins: I will be far harsher than my father
decisions.reason: The boast compares the smallest part of the new king with the thickest part of the old one. Rehoboam's least effort will weigh more on them than Solomon's greatest.

decisions.choice: my little [finger]
decisions.reason: The word means "my little one" or "my smallness"; the word for finger is not written but is understood. It appears only here and in the parallel at 2 Chronicles 10:10.

decisions.choice: loins: the waist and hips
decisions.reason: The word names the middle of the body, where a belt is worn, the thickest part of a man.

decisions.choice: the young men tell Rehoboam twice what to say
decisions.reason: "Thus you shall say ... thus you shall speak" frames the people's words and then the answer the young men put into his mouth, which runs on through verse 11.

decisions.choice: waist
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "waist", the ordinary word for this part of the body; Literal keeps "loins".

decisions.choice: I will be much harder on you than he was
decisions.reason: Readable adds a plain sentence that explains the boast. Verse 11 says the same in other words.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה אָבִי֙ הֶעְמִ֤יס עֲלֵיכֶם֙ עֹ֣ל כָּבֵ֔ד וַאֲנִ֖י אוֹסִ֣יף עַֽל־עֻלְּכֶ֑ם אָבִ֗י יִסַּ֤ר אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּשּׁוֹטִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֕י אֲיַסֵּ֥ר אֶתְכֶ֖ם בָּעַקְרַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And now my father loaded on you a yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with the whips, and I will discipline you with the scorpions.

en.L: And now, my father loaded a heavy yoke on you, but I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.'"
en.B: So then: my father laid a heavy yoke on you, but I will make your yoke heavier still. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions.'"
en.R: My father put a heavy load on you, but I will make it even heavier. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions, which hurt far more!'"

decisions.choice: scorpions: a far crueler punishment than whips
alternatives: a whip fitted with barbs or spikes
a picture of the scorpion's sting
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for the scorpion. It may name a kind of whip fitted with barbs or spikes that bit into the skin, or the scorpion's sting may simply be set against the whip as a picture of far worse pain. Either way the meaning is the same: Rehoboam will punish much more harshly than Solomon did.

decisions.choice: disciplined: punished in order to correct
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a father correcting a son (Deuteronomy 8:5; Proverbs 19:18). Here it names the harsh treatment of forced laborers by those set over them.

decisions.choice: and now: the conclusion of the boast
decisions.reason: "And now" draws the conclusion from the boast of verse 10 and spells out what it means.

decisions.choice: which hurt far more
decisions.reason: Readable adds what the picture of the scorpion means, so that the threat is clear without a note.

source.text: וַיָּב֨וֹא יָרָבְעָ֧ם וְכָל־הָעָ֛ם אֶל־רְחַבְעָ֖ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר שׁ֥וּבוּ אֵלַ֖י בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Jeroboam and all the people to Rehoboam on the day the third, as had spoken the king, saying, Return to me on the day the third.

en.L: And Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had spoken, saying, "Return to me on the third day."
en.B: On the third day Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam, as the king had told them: "Return to me on the third day."
en.R: On the third day Jeroboam and all the people came back to Rehoboam, just as the king had told them to do.

decisions.choice: came: the form marked to be read aloud is singular
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) and the form the scribes marked to be read aloud (qere) spell the verb "came" differently, and the marked form is singular, agreeing with Jeroboam, named first. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: on the third day: the time Rehoboam had set
decisions.reason: The repeated words stress that the people did exactly what the king asked (verse 5). They kept their part; the king's answer follows.

decisions.choice: the king's words are not repeated
decisions.reason: Readable says that the people did as they were told instead of quoting the king again.

source.text: וַיַּ֧עַן הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶת־הָעָ֖ם קָשָׁ֑ה וַֽיַּעֲזֹ֛ב אֶת־עֲצַ֥ת הַזְּקֵנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְעָצֻֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered the king the people hard, and he abandoned the counsel of the elders which they had counseled him.

en.L: And the king answered the people harshly, and he forsook the counsel of the elders that they had counseled him.
en.B: The king gave the people a harsh answer. He rejected the advice the elders had given him.
en.R: The king answered the people harshly. He did not follow the older men's advice.

decisions.choice: harshly: the same word as the "hard" service of verse 4
decisions.reason: The people asked to be freed from "hard" service; the king answers them "hard". The repeated word shows that he meets their complaint with more of what they complained of.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כַּעֲצַ֤ת הַיְלָדִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אָבִי֙ הִכְבִּ֣יד אֶֽת־עֻלְּכֶ֔ם וַאֲנִ֖י אֹסִ֣יף עַֽל־עֻלְּכֶ֑ם אָבִ֗י יִסַּ֤ר אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּשּׁוֹטִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֕י אֲיַסֵּ֥ר אֶתְכֶ֖ם בָּעַקְרַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he spoke to them according to [the] counsel of the young men, saying, My father made heavy your yoke, and I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with the whips, and I will discipline you with the scorpions.

en.L: And he spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, "My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions."
en.B: He spoke to them as the young men had advised: "My father made your yoke heavy, but I will make your yoke heavier still. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions."
en.R: He followed the young men's advice and said, "My father put a heavy load on you, but I will make it even heavier. My father punished you with whips, but I will punish you with scorpions, which hurt far more!"

decisions.choice: the young men's words repeated almost exactly
decisions.reason: Rehoboam repeats verse 11 nearly word for word. He leaves out the boast about his little finger (verse 10), and he says "made heavy", the people's own word in verse 10, instead of "loaded".

decisions.choice: scorpions: as in verse 11
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, a far crueler punishment than whips.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־שָׁמַ֥ע הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־הָעָ֑ם כִּֽי־הָיְתָ֤ה סִבָּה֙ מֵעִ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה לְמַ֜עַן הָקִ֣ים אֶת־דְּבָר֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ בְּיַד֙ אֲחִיָּ֣ה הַשִּׁילֹנִ֔י אֶל־יָרָבְעָ֖ם בֶּן־נְבָֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: And not listened the king to the people, for it was a turn from with Yahweh, in order to establish his word which spoke Yahweh by [the] hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

en.L: And the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turn [of events] from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in order to establish {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
en.B: So the king did not listen to the people, for this turn of events came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to fulfill the word {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
en.R: So the king did not listen to the people. This was {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s doing. He was making {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word come true, the message {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had given to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah, the prophet from Shiloh.

decisions.choice: a turn of events: something brought about
decisions.reason: The word appears only here and in the parallel, 2 Chronicles 10:15. It comes from the verb "to turn" and means an outcome caused by someone. The Hebrew says it came "from with the LORD": he brought it about.

decisions.choice: Rehoboam's own choice serves the LORD's purpose
decisions.reason: Rehoboam chose his answer himself (verses 8 and 13), yet the writer says the outcome came from the LORD. The LORD had announced that he would tear ten tribes from Solomon's son because of Solomon's idolatry (11:11-13, 31-36).

decisions.choice: Ahijah the Shilonite: the prophet from Shiloh
decisions.reason: Ahijah came from Shiloh, where the tabernacle once stood (1 Samuel 1:3). He tore his new cloak into twelve pieces and gave ten to Jeroboam as a sign (11:29-39).

decisions.choice: by the hand of: through
decisions.reason: God's word comes "by the hand of" a prophet when the prophet speaks it for him.

decisions.choice: the prophet from Shiloh
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the Shilonite" and says that Ahijah was a prophet (11:29).

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּ֠י לֹֽא־שָׁמַ֣ע הַמֶּלֶךְ֮ אֲלֵיהֶם֒ וַיָּשִׁ֣בוּ הָעָ֣ם אֶת־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּבָ֣ר׀לֵאמֹ֡ר מַה־לָּנוּ֩ חֵ֨לֶק בְּדָוִ֜ד וְלֹֽא־נַחֲלָ֣ה בְּבֶן־יִשַׁ֗י לְאֹהָלֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַתָּ֕ה רְאֵ֥ה בֵיתְךָ֖ דָּוִ֑ד וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְאֹהָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw all Israel that not listened the king to them, and brought back the people [to] the king word, saying, What [is] to us portion in David? And not inheritance in [the] son of Jesse! To your tents, Israel! Now see your house, David! And went Israel to his tents.

en.L: And all Israel saw that the king did not listen to them, and the people returned a word to the king, saying, \q "What portion [is there] for us in David? \q And no inheritance in the son of Jesse! \q To your tents, Israel! Now see to your own house, David!" \q And Israel went to its tents.
en.B: When all Israel saw that the king would not listen to them, the people answered the king: \q "What part do we have in David? \q We have no inheritance in Jesse's son! \q To your tents, Israel! Now look after your own house, David!" \q So Israel went home.
en.R: All Israel saw that the king would not listen to them. So they answered the king, \q "We have no share in David! \q We get nothing from Jesse's son! \q Go home, Israel! David, look after your own family now!" \q So the people of Israel went home.

decisions.choice: the cry of Sheba's revolt against David
decisions.reason: The words echo the cry of Sheba son of Bichri when he led Israel away from David (2 Samuel 20:1). Here the first line is a question ("What portion do we have?") instead of a statement ("We have no portion"), "each man" is missing, and a last line is added: "Now see to your own house, David!" What Sheba began, the northern tribes now finish.

decisions.choice: no portion, no inheritance: David's house is nothing to us
decisions.reason: A portion and an inheritance are a share in family land. The tribes say they have no stake in David's family and owe it nothing.

decisions.choice: to your tents: go home
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from Israel's days of living in tents. It breaks up the assembly: each man goes home, and the people refuse the king (2 Samuel 20:1; 1 Kings 8:66).

decisions.choice: see to your own house, David: let David's family rule its own tribe
decisions.reason: "House" means David's family and line of kings. The tribes tell the house of David to look after Judah, its own tribe, and leave the rest of Israel alone.

decisions.choice: the son of Jesse: said with contempt
decisions.reason: Calling David "the son of Jesse" instead of by his name or title is a slight, as in 1 Samuel 20:27 and 22:7-9 and 2 Samuel 20:1.

decisions.choice: the cry set in three lines
decisions.reason: The people's answer is a short poem; its lines follow the Hebrew divisions, with the last two calls sharing a line. Literal and Balanced keep the wording of 2 Samuel 20:1 where the Hebrew is the same ("portion", "part", "inheritance", "Jesse's son"); the narrative closing the verse stands as its own line.

decisions.choice: We have no share; We get nothing; Go home; family
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a plain statement, as in 2 Samuel 20:1, and explains "to your tents" and "house".

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם רְחַבְעָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Israel, the ones dwelling in [the] cities of Judah, reigned over them Rehoboam.

en.L: But [as for] the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel who were living in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
en.B: But Rehoboam reigned over the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who lived in the towns of Judah.
en.R: But Rehoboam still ruled over the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} who lived in the towns of Judah.

decisions.choice: the Israelites: here the people of all the tribes
decisions.reason: In this verse "Israelites" still has its wide sense, the people descended from Jacob, and so includes the people of Judah and any from the northern tribes who had settled in Judah's towns. From verse 20 on, "Israel" alone names the northern kingdom.

decisions.choice: but: set against the departure of Israel
decisions.reason: The sentence puts "the Israelites who lived in the towns of Judah" first, to set them against the rest of Israel, who had just gone home (verse 16).

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers both cities and small walled towns. "Towns" fits most of the places in Judah.

decisions.choice: still
decisions.reason: Readable adds "still" to show that Judah stayed with Rehoboam while the rest went away.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם אֶת־אֲדֹרָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הַמַּ֔ס וַיִּרְגְּמ֨וּ כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל בּ֛וֹ אֶ֖בֶן וַיָּמֹ֑ת וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם הִתְאַמֵּץ֙ לַעֲל֣וֹת בַּמֶּרְכָּבָ֔ה לָנ֖וּס יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent the king Rehoboam Adoram, who [was] over the forced labor, and stoned all Israel him [with] stone, and he died; and the king Rehoboam made himself strong to go up into the chariot to flee [to] Jerusalem.

en.L: And King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who [was] over the forced labor, and all Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. And King Rehoboam made haste to go up into the chariot to flee [to] Jerusalem.
en.B: King Rehoboam then sent Adoram, the officer in charge of the forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam managed to get up into his chariot and escape to Jerusalem.
en.R: Then King Rehoboam sent Adoram to the people. Adoram was in charge of the men who were forced to work for the king. But all the people of Israel threw stones at him until he died. King Rehoboam hurried to jump into his chariot, and he escaped to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Adoram, over the forced labor
decisions.reason: The forced labor was the system of work gangs that built Solomon's temple, palace and cities (5:27-28; 9:15). Adoram is probably the same man as Adoniram, who held this post under Solomon (4:6; 5:28); the shorter form of his name is used in 2 Samuel 20:24. Sending the man in charge of the very burden the people complained of was a provocation, whatever Rehoboam meant by it.

decisions.choice: made haste: managed with effort
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself strong. Here it describes the king pulling himself together and getting into his chariot just in time; it was a narrow escape.

decisions.choice: stoned him: put him to death as a group
decisions.reason: Stoning was a death carried out by a whole community. Here it shows that the people as a body rejected the king's authority.

decisions.choice: the men who were forced to work for the king
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "the forced labor" was.

decisions.choice: his chariot
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the chariot"; it was the king's own.

source.text: וַיִּפְשְׁע֤וּ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּבֵ֣ית דָּוִ֔ד עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And rebelled Israel against [the] house of David until the day the this.

en.L: So Israel has rebelled against the house of David to this day.
en.B: So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.
en.R: So Israel turned against the family of David, and it has stayed separate from it to this day.

decisions.choice: rebelled: broke away from its ruler
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a people throwing off the rule of its overlord, as Moab and Edom later rebelled against Israel and Judah (2 Kings 1:1; 8:20). It describes a political break, not only a quarrel.

decisions.choice: to this day: the writer's own day
decisions.reason: As at 8:8, "to this day" means the time when this account was written. The northern kingdom never returned to the house of David.

decisions.choice: the house of David: the royal line promised to David
decisions.reason: The LORD had promised David a lasting house, a line of kings (2 Samuel 7:16). The split leaves that line ruling Judah only, as the LORD had said (11:13, 36).

decisions.choice: turned against ... stayed separate
decisions.reason: Readable puts the lasting state that the Hebrew verb describes in two plain verbs.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י כִּשְׁמֹ֤עַ כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּֽי־שָׁ֣ב יָרָבְעָ֔ם וַֽיִּשְׁלְח֗וּ וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ אֶל־הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה וַיַּמְלִ֥יכוּ אֹת֖וֹ עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לֹ֤א הָיָה֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י בֵית־דָּוִ֔ד זוּלָתִ֥י שֵֽׁבֶט־יְהוּדָ֖ה לְבַדּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when heard all Israel that had returned Jeroboam, and they sent and called him to the congregation and made king him over all Israel; not was [one] after [the] house of David except [the] tribe of Judah by itself.

en.L: And it happened, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, that they sent and called him to the congregation and made him king over all Israel. There was none following the house of David except the tribe of Judah by itself.
en.B: When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they sent for him, summoned him before the congregation, and made him king over all Israel. No one followed the house of David except the tribe of Judah alone.
en.R: When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had come back, they sent for him and called him to their gathering. There they made him king over all Israel. Only the tribe of Judah stayed loyal to David's family.

decisions.choice: Israel: from here on, the northern kingdom; Judah: the southern kingdom
decisions.reason: Until now "Israel" has named the whole people and the kingdom of David and Solomon. From this verse on, Kings uses "Israel" for the kingdom of the northern tribes ruled by Jeroboam and his successors, and "Judah" for the kingdom ruled by David's line from Jerusalem. The wider sense still appears in some phrases, such as "the LORD, the God of Israel".

decisions.choice: Jeroboam had returned: the northern assembly's side of the story
decisions.reason: Verses 3 and 12 already have Jeroboam with the people at Shechem. This verse may tell how the tribes, once Rehoboam had been rejected, formally called Jeroboam to their assembly and made him king. See the note at verse 3.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Judah alone: Benjamin was also joined to Judah
decisions.reason: The next verse counts Benjamin with Judah. The prophet had said that one tribe would be left to David's line (11:13, 32, 36); Judah was that tribe, and part of Benjamin, where Jerusalem lay on the border, stayed with it.

decisions.choice: the congregation: the tribes formally assembled
decisions.reason: The word names Israel gathered as a body to act together. Here the assembly of the northern tribes makes Jeroboam king.

decisions.choice: Israel and Judah at every level
decisions.reason: The names are kept as the Hebrew has them at every level, without "the northern kingdom" or "the southern kingdom"; the meaning decision explains them. Readable says "gathering" for the congregation, as the Numbers to Ruth terms allow.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א רְחַבְעָם֮ יְרוּשָׁלִַם֒ וַיַּקְהֵל֩ אֶת־כָּל־בֵּ֨ית יְהוּדָ֜ה וְאֶת־שֵׁ֣בֶט בִּנְיָמִ֗ן מֵאָ֨ה וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף בָּח֖וּר עֹשֵׂ֣ה מִלְחָמָ֑ה לְהִלָּחֵם֙ עִם־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְהָשִׁיב֙ אֶת־הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה לִרְחַבְעָ֖ם בֶּן־שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And came Rehoboam [to] Jerusalem, and he assembled all [the] house of Judah and [the] tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen [men], doers of war, to fight with [the] house of Israel, to bring back the kingship to Rehoboam son of Solomon.

en.L: And Rehoboam came [to] Jerusalem and assembled all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, 180,000 chosen [men], makers of war, to fight with the house of Israel, to bring back the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
en.B: When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he mustered the whole house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, 180,000 picked warriors, to fight against the house of Israel and regain the kingdom for Rehoboam son of Solomon.
en.R: When Rehoboam got back to Jerusalem, he gathered 180,000 of the best soldiers from all the people of Judah and from the tribe of Benjamin. He wanted to fight against Israel and win back the kingdom for himself, Rehoboam son of Solomon.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Benjamin with Judah
decisions.reason: Benjamin lay between Judah and the northern tribes, and Jerusalem stood on its border with Judah (Joshua 18:16, 28). Though Saul had come from Benjamin, at least part of the tribe now stayed with the house of David.

decisions.choice: 180,000: "thousand" as written
decisions.reason: The number is given as the Hebrew has it. As in the census lists of Numbers, the word for "thousand" can also name a military unit, which would make the force much smaller.

decisions.choice: chosen men, makers of war: picked fighting men
decisions.reason: "Chosen" means men picked for service, usually young and fit; "makers of war" means trained soldiers.

decisions.choice: came: the form marked to be read aloud is singular
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) and the form the scribes marked to be read aloud (qere) spell the verb "came" differently; the marked form is singular, agreeing with Rehoboam. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: for himself, Rehoboam son of Solomon
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long sentence and makes clear that Rehoboam meant to win back the kingdom for himself.

source.text: וַיְהִי֙ דְּבַ֣ר הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶל־שְׁמַעְיָ֥ה אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And was [the] word of the God to Shemaiah, [the] man of the God, saying,

en.L: And the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
en.B: But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God:
en.R: But God gave this message to Shemaiah the man of God:

decisions.choice: the man of God: a prophet
decisions.reason: "Man of God" is a title for a prophet who speaks God's word (1 Samuel 2:27; 9:6-10). Shemaiah appears again in 2 Chronicles 12:5-8, 15.

decisions.choice: but: God stops the war
decisions.reason: The word of God comes just as Rehoboam is ready to march, and it turns the story.

source.text: אֱמֹ֗ר אֶל־רְחַבְעָ֤ם בֶּן־שְׁלֹמֹה֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה וְאֶל־כָּל־בֵּ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִנְיָמִ֑ין וְיֶ֥תֶר הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all [the] house of Judah and Benjamin and [the] rest of the people, saying,

en.L: "Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and the rest of the people, saying,
en.B: "Speak to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to the whole house of Judah and Benjamin, and to everyone else among the people, and tell them,
en.R: "Speak to Rehoboam son of Solomon, the king of Judah. Speak also to all the people of Judah and Benjamin and to everyone else who is with them. Tell them,

decisions.choice: king of Judah: God's word names Rehoboam king of Judah only
decisions.reason: For the first time Rehoboam is called "king of Judah". God's message itself accepts the division of the kingdom.

decisions.choice: the rest of the people: others gathered with Judah and Benjamin
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean people of other tribes who lived in Judah (verse 17), or simply everyone else in Rehoboam's army.

source.text: כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֡ה לֹֽא־תַעֲלוּ֩ וְלֹא־תִלָּ֨חֲמ֜וּן עִם־אֲחֵיכֶ֣ם בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שׁ֚וּבוּ אִ֣ישׁ לְבֵית֔וֹ כִּ֧י מֵאִתִּ֛י נִהְיָ֖ה הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶת־דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּשֻׁ֥בוּ לָלֶ֖כֶת כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh, Not you shall go up and not you shall fight with your brothers, [the] sons of Israel; return each to his house, for from with me has come about the thing the this. And they listened to [the] word of Yahweh and turned back to go according to [the] word of Yahweh.

en.L: 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: You shall not go up, and you shall not fight with your brothers, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel. Return, each man to his house, for this thing has come about from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'" And they listened to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and turned back to go [home], according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Do not go up to fight against your relatives, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Go home, every one of you, for this thing has come from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'" So they heeded the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and went back home, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.
en.R: 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Do not go to war against your relatives, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. All of you go home. I am the one who made this happen.'" So they obeyed the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and went home, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told them.

decisions.choice: this has come from me: the LORD owns the division
decisions.reason: As verse 15 says, the split of the kingdom is the LORD's doing. To fight it would be to fight against him.

decisions.choice: your brothers: your own kin
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means fellow members of one people, descended from Jacob's sons. The war would be a war within one family.

decisions.choice: go up and fight: march to war
decisions.reason: To "go up" is often to set out on a campaign; the two verbs together mean "march out to fight".

decisions.choice: they listened and turned back
decisions.reason: The army obeys at once. The story of the division ends with Judah accepting God's word, though there was fighting between the two kingdoms later (14:30; 15:6).

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "relatives" to show that "brothers" means kin, not only brothers born of the same parents; Literal keeps "brothers".

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD; The LORD says this; This is what the LORD says
decisions.reason: The prophet's formula is worded the same way at each level throughout Samuel, Kings and Chronicles.

source.text: וַיִּ֨בֶן יָרָבְעָ֧ם אֶת־שְׁכֶ֛ם בְּהַ֥ר אֶפְרַ֖יִם וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב בָּ֑הּ וַיֵּצֵ֣א מִשָּׁ֔ם וַיִּ֖בֶן אֶת־פְּנוּאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And built Jeroboam Shechem in [the] hill country of Ephraim and dwelt in it, and went out from there and built Penuel.

en.L: And Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived in it; and he went out from there and built Penuel.
en.B: Jeroboam fortified Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. From there he went out and fortified Penuel.
en.R: Jeroboam made the town of Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim stronger, and he lived there. Then he went out from there and made the town of Penuel stronger too.

decisions.choice: built: rebuilt and fortified
decisions.reason: Shechem and Penuel were old towns, so "built" means that Jeroboam rebuilt them and strengthened their walls. Both had been destroyed in Gideon's and Abimelech's days (Judges 8:17; 9:45).

decisions.choice: Penuel: a town east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Penuel lay by the Jabbok River east of the Jordan, where Jacob wrestled with God (Genesis 32:31-32). Fortifying it guarded the eastern part of Jeroboam's kingdom.

decisions.choice: went out from there
decisions.reason: This may mean that Jeroboam went out on a campaign from Shechem, or that he later moved his residence. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: fortified; made stronger
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "built" means for towns that already stood.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יָרָבְעָ֖ם בְּלִבּ֑וֹ עַתָּ֛ה תָּשׁ֥וּב הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית דָּוִֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jeroboam in his heart, Now will return the kingdom to [the] house of David.

en.L: And Jeroboam said in his heart, "Now the kingdom will return to the house of David.
en.B: Jeroboam thought to himself, "As things are, the kingdom will go back to the house of David.
en.R: But Jeroboam was worried. He thought, "The way things are going, the kingdom will go back to David's family.

decisions.choice: said in his heart: thought to himself
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought; to say something in one's heart is to think it without speaking.

decisions.choice: now: as matters stand
decisions.reason: "Now" here points to the present state of things: if nothing changes, the kingdom will go back to David's house. Jeroboam fears this, though the LORD had promised him a lasting house if he obeyed (11:38).

decisions.choice: was worried
decisions.reason: Readable states the fear that the following words express.

source.text: אִֽם־יַעֲלֶ֣ה׀הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה לַעֲשׂ֨וֹת זְבָחִ֤ים בְּבֵית־יְהוָה֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְ֠שָׁב לֵ֣ב הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ אֶל־אֲדֹ֣נֵיהֶ֔ם אֶל־רְחַבְעָ֖ם מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַהֲרָגֻ֕נִי וְשָׁ֖בוּ אֶל־רְחַבְעָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: If goes up the people the this to make sacrifices in [the] house of Yahweh in Jerusalem, then will return [the] heart of the people the this to their lord, to Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.

en.L: If this people goes up to make sacrifices in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem, then the heart of this people will turn back to their lord, to Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah."
en.B: If these people go up to offer sacrifices at the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem, their hearts will turn back to their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me and go back to Rehoboam king of Judah."
en.R: If these people keep going to Jerusalem to offer sacrifices at the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, they will start to feel loyal again to their old master, Rehoboam king of Judah. They will kill me and go back to King Rehoboam."

decisions.choice: the house of the LORD in Jerusalem: the temple Solomon built
decisions.reason: Solomon had built the temple as the place where the LORD's name would dwell (8:29), and the law tells Israel to bring its sacrifices to the place the LORD chooses (Deuteronomy 12:5-14). The great festivals drew people from every tribe to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the heart will turn back: loyalty will return
decisions.reason: The heart stands for will and loyalty. Worship in Rehoboam's city would draw the people's loyalty back to Rehoboam.

decisions.choice: their lord: their rightful master
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for a master or ruler. Jeroboam fears that the people will come to see Rehoboam as their rightful king again.

decisions.choice: the temple of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable calls the house of the LORD the temple, the usual word for it.

source.text: וַיִּוָּעַ֣ץ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיַּ֕עַשׂ שְׁנֵ֖י עֶגְלֵ֣י זָהָ֑ב וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם רַב־לָכֶם֙ מֵעֲל֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם הִנֵּ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And took counsel the king and made two calves of gold, and said to them, Much for you from going up [to] Jerusalem; here your gods, Israel, who brought you up from [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And the king took counsel and made two calves of gold. And he said to them, "[It is] enough for you, going up [to] Jerusalem. Here [are] your gods, O Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt."
en.B: So the king took counsel and made two golden calves. He said to the people, "You have gone up to Jerusalem long enough. Israel, here are your gods, who brought you up from the land of Egypt!"
en.R: So the king asked for advice. Then he made two statues of young bulls out of gold. He told the people, "You have been going to Jerusalem long enough. Israel, here are your gods who brought you out of Egypt!"

decisions.choice: Aaron's golden calf (Exodus 32:4, 8)
decisions.reason: Jeroboam's words repeat what the people said of the golden calf at Mount Sinai: "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt" (Exodus 32:4, 8). The one difference is the first word: here "here are" instead of "these are". Jeroboam's new worship begins with Israel's first great sin.

decisions.choice: your gods ... who brought you up: plural
alternatives: your God, who brought you up
decisions.reason: The word for God has a plural form, and here the verb "brought up" is plural too, so the sentence speaks of gods, as in Exodus 32:4. Jeroboam may have meant the calves as thrones or pedestals for the LORD, who rescued Israel from Egypt, but the writer counts them as other gods (14:9).

decisions.choice: enough for you, going up to Jerusalem: you have gone there long enough
alternatives: it is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The same phrase means "you have stayed long enough" in Deuteronomy 1:6 and 2:3, and that sense is followed: Jeroboam tells the people that their journeys to Jerusalem are over. It can also mean "it is too much trouble for you", which would present the change as a kindness.

decisions.choice: calves: young bulls
decisions.reason: A calf here is a young bull, a common picture of strength and of divine power in the ancient Near East. Bethel and Dan had both been holy places before (Genesis 28:19; Judges 18:30-31).

decisions.choice: the wording of Exodus 32:4
decisions.reason: Each level reuses its own wording of Exodus 32:4, changing "these are" to "here are" at Literal and Balanced; Readable already has "here are" there.

decisions.choice: statues of young bulls out of gold
decisions.reason: Readable explains "calves" as in Exodus 32:4.

source.text: וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת־הָאֶחָ֖ד בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֑ל וְאֶת־הָאֶחָ֖ד נָתַ֥ן בְּדָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he set the one in Bethel, and the one he put in Dan.

en.L: And he set the one in Bethel, and the [other] one he put in Dan.
en.B: He set up one in Bethel, and the other he put in Dan.
en.R: He put one of them in the town of Bethel and the other in the town of Dan.

decisions.choice: Bethel and Dan: the southern and northern edges of the kingdom
decisions.reason: Bethel lay near the border with Judah, on the road to Jerusalem; Jacob had worshiped there (Genesis 28:19; 35:1-15). Dan lay in the far north, where the tribe of Dan had set up an idol and its own priests (Judges 18:29-31). The two shrines covered the kingdom from end to end.

decisions.choice: the town of
decisions.reason: Readable says that Bethel and Dan were towns.

source.text: וַיְהִ֛י הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה לְחַטָּ֑את וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ הָעָ֛ם לִפְנֵ֥י הָאֶחָ֖ד עַד־דָּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And became the thing the this a sin, and went the people before the one as far as Dan.

en.L: And this thing became a sin, and the people went before the one [calf] as far as Dan.
en.B: This thing became a sin. The people went as far as Dan to worship before the one there.
en.R: This became a sin. The people even went all the way to Dan to worship the calf there.

decisions.choice: this thing became a sin: the sin of Jeroboam
decisions.reason: From here on Kings measures the kings of Israel by "the sin of Jeroboam", the worship he set up at Bethel and Dan, and the sin he made Israel commit (14:16; 15:26, 30, 34).

decisions.choice: before the one, as far as Dan
alternatives: before the one at Bethel and before the other as far as Dan
decisions.reason: The sentence names only one calf, at Dan. Some think words about Bethel dropped out of the Hebrew text. Read as it stands, it says that the people traveled all the way to Dan, at the far north, to worship the calf there.

decisions.choice: went before: went to worship before
decisions.reason: To go "before" an image means to come into its presence to worship it, perhaps in procession.

decisions.choice: to worship
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say why the people went before the calf. Readable adds "even" and "all the way" for the long journey implied by "as far as Dan".

source.text: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית בָּמ֑וֹת וַיַּ֤עַשׂ כֹּֽהֲנִים֙ מִקְצ֣וֹת הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־הָי֖וּ מִבְּנֵ֥י לֵוִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made [a] house of high places, and he made priests from [the] ends of the people, who were not from [the] sons of Levi.

en.L: And he made a house of high places, and he made priests from [the] whole range of the people, who were not from the sons of Levi.
en.B: He also made shrines on the high places and appointed priests from all sorts of people, who were not Levites.
en.R: Jeroboam also built hilltop shrines. And he chose priests from all kinds of people, men who were not from the tribe of Levi.

decisions.choice: a house of high places: shrine buildings at the high places
decisions.reason: A high place was a place of worship, often on a hill, with an altar. A "house" there was a shrine building; the singular probably stands for many such shrines (13:32).

decisions.choice: from the whole range of the people
alternatives: from the lowest of the people
decisions.reason: The phrase means "from the ends of the people", that is, from anywhere among them, from any family at all. It does not mean the poorest or lowest people. The point is that they were not chosen from the priestly tribe.

decisions.choice: not from the sons of Levi: not of the priestly tribe
decisions.reason: The law gave the priesthood to Aaron's descendants and the service of the sanctuary to the tribe of Levi (Numbers 3:10; 18:1-7; Deuteronomy 18:1-5). Jeroboam's priests had no such claim.

decisions.choice: hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: Readable says "hilltop shrines" for the high places, as throughout Samuel, Kings and Chronicles.

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ יָרָבְעָ֣ם׀חָ֡ג בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁמִינִ֣י בַּחֲמִשָּֽׁה־עָשָׂר֩ י֨וֹם׀לַחֹ֜דֶשׁ כֶּחָ֣ג׀אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּיהוּדָ֗ה וַיַּ֨עַל֙ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כֵּ֤ן עָשָׂה֙ בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֔ל לְזַבֵּ֖חַ לָעֲגָלִ֣ים אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֑ה וְהֶעֱמִיד֙ בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔ל אֶת־כֹּהֲנֵ֥י הַבָּמ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: And made Jeroboam a festival in the month the eighth, on [the] fifteenth day of the month, like the festival which [was] in Judah, and he went up on the altar; so he did in Bethel, to sacrifice to the calves which he had made; and he stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places which he had made.

en.L: And Jeroboam made a festival in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the festival that [was] in Judah, and he went up on the altar. So he did in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves that he had made; and he stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places that he had made.
en.B: Jeroboam instituted a festival on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the festival held in Judah, and he went up to the altar. He did this in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves he had made. And in Bethel he installed the priests of the high places he had made.
en.R: Jeroboam started a festival on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. It was like the festival held in Judah. He went up to the altar at Bethel and offered sacrifices to the calves he had made. He also put the priests he had chosen for the hilltop shrines to work at Bethel.

decisions.choice: the festival in Judah: the Festival of Booths
decisions.reason: The festival held in Judah began on the fifteenth day of the seventh month: the Festival of Booths, the great autumn feast at the end of the harvest (Leviticus 23:33-36; Deuteronomy 16:13-15). Solomon had dedicated the temple at it (8:2, 65). Jeroboam held his copy a month later.

decisions.choice: went up on the altar
decisions.reason: The verb form can mean either "he went up" or "he offered up"; the two are spelled alike. The altar was high and was approached by steps or a ramp, and the king went up on it to offer. Either way, Jeroboam himself acts as priest at his altar. The same words recur in verse 33.

decisions.choice: that he had made: the work of Jeroboam's hands
decisions.reason: The writer keeps saying what Jeroboam "made": calves, high places, priests, an altar, a festival (verses 28-33). Everything in this worship is of his own making.

decisions.choice: the altar at Bethel; put to work
decisions.reason: Readable joins the altar and Bethel in one sentence and says plainly that Jeroboam gave the priests their posts at Bethel.

source.text: וַיַּ֜עַל עַֽל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֣חַ׀אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֣ה בְּבֵֽית־אֵ֗ל בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁמִינִ֔י בַּחֹ֖דֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּדָ֣א מִלִּבּ֑וֹ וַיַּ֤עַשׂ חָג֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּ֥עַל עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לְהַקְטִֽיר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he went up on the altar which he had made in Bethel on [the] fifteenth day in the month the eighth, in the month which he had devised from his heart, and he made a festival for [the] sons of Israel and went up on the altar to make smoke.

en.L: And he went up on the altar that he had made in Bethel on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, in the month that he had devised from his own heart; and he made a festival for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and he went up on the altar to burn incense.
en.B: He went up to the altar he had made in Bethel on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, the month he had invented on his own. He instituted a festival for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and went up to the altar to burn incense.
en.R: On the fifteenth day of the eighth month, Jeroboam went up to the altar he had built at Bethel. He had made up that date himself. He started a festival for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and he went up to the altar to burn incense.

decisions.choice: devised: made up
decisions.reason: The verb means to invent; it is used of a false report made up by an enemy (Nehemiah 6:8). The date had no command of God behind it.

decisions.choice: from his own heart
decisions.reason: The reading the scribes marked to be read aloud (qere) is "from his heart"; the written consonants (ketiv) can be read "by himself". Both say that Jeroboam chose the month on his own authority.

decisions.choice: to burn incense: to make offerings go up in smoke
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke, used of incense and of the fat of sacrifices. The story goes straight on in 13:1, where Jeroboam is standing at the altar to make his offering when the man of God arrives.

decisions.choice: went up on the altar: as in verse 32
decisions.reason: The same words as in verse 32 frame this verse at its start and end, and lead into the next chapter.

decisions.choice: made up that date himself
decisions.reason: Readable says "date" because the point is the day and month of the festival.
